title: DevX tutorial remediation scratchpad
content:
Notes to self - quick, messy, actionable.

Context:
- Follow-up to user reports that the "Getting started: SDK + Hosted API" tutorial fails on step 4 (auth + streaming). Multiple folks hit this in the last week.
- Repro shows two distinct failure modes: (A) auth token not picked up by local env flow, (B) stream handler error (chunk parsing) when using node14 in sample app.
- Related GH issue and small PR attempts listed above. Need consolidated remediation plan and an ordered list of patches we can push this sprint.

Repro steps (fresh laptop, macOS Monterey):
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/tree/tutorial-samples
2) cd tutorial-samples/basic-node
3) npm i (node 14.x)
4) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxx (user used .env; tutorial shows export but sample uses dotenv in code)
5) node app.js -> behavior: immediate crash with JSON parse error OR token undefined depending on env loading order

Hypothesis / root cause(s):
- Mixed guidance: tutorial text tells user to set REDWOOD_API_KEY via shell export but sample app uses dotenv. If user follows tutorial exactly they may not create .env and code tries to read process.env earlier -> undefined.
- Stream parsing bug: our example stream handler assumes each record is complete JSON per chunk; runtime (node14) sometimes emits partial frames and we try JSON.parse on incomplete data -> throw.
- Node version mismatch not surfaced: tutorial requests "node >= 16" in sidebar but the sample package.json has engines: 14 -> confusion.

Quick fixes (short-term, hot path) - aim to ship in <48h:
- Update sample app to: 1) prefer process.env directly and add a clear inline fallback comment; 2) include a tiny `if (!process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY) { console.error(...) ; process.exit(1) }` with helpful text and link to how to get a key.
- Replace simple chunk JSON.parse with a buffered-accumulator that splits on line delimiters and robustly attempts parse only on complete records. Add a small utility in sample-app/helpers/stream-safe.js with tests.
- Align package.json engine to >=16 and update tutorial text to call out recommended Node LTS explicitly.
- Update tutorial prose: explicit step to run `node -v` and a troubleshooting section for env vs dotenv.

Sample-app checklist (deliverables):
- [ ] code: sample/basic-node/app.js: replace parsing logic + env guard (owner: Diego)
- [ ] tests: add unit test for streaming util that simulates partial chunks (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] docs: tutorial page edits—auth section, node version note, troubleshooting snippet (owner: Luca)
- [ ] CI: add a tiny smoke test that runs sample app against a mock server in GH Actions matrix for node14/16 to ensure we surface version issues (owner: Diego, supports: infra)
- [ ] release PR: one single PR linking code + docs changes (target: merge after review so users get consistent update)

Acceptance criteria (how we'll know it's fixed):
- Fresh-cloned tutorial and sample app run from first-to-last step with no unhandled exceptions on node16 and show explicit error on missing env variable.
- GH issue #329 marked resolved with user confirmation (or at minimum, automated smoke test in actions passes).
- No follow-ups in Slack by EOD +2 on the update (informal metric).

Edge cases / follow-ups (nice-to-have):
- Add short snippet showing how to use dotenv and a note on not checking .env into git.
- Add one-liner for Windows PowerShell env var set to reduce friction for Windows devs.
- Consider adding a small containerized example (Dockerfile) to avoid local env friction for workshops.

Timeline + estimation (rough):
- Diego: 2-3h to patch sample app and add buffer util + unit tests
- Aisha: 2h to write tests and run locally across versions
- Luca: 1h to update tutorial text and screenshots if needed
- Review + merge: 1-2h depending on reviewer availability
Total: ~6-8 engineer-hours.

Blocking items / questions:
- Who on docs reviews should sign-off on wording? Pinged @Luca but need product voice approval if we change wording around token security.
- Do we want to backport a minimal CHANGELOG entry for the sample-app fix? (probably yes)
- Is shipping a CI matrix with node14 required? We can run matrix but docs will say node16 recommended.

Quick commit plan (branch names, PR title):
- branch: diego/devx/tutorial-stream-fix-2026-03
- commit 1: sample: env guard + engine bump
- commit 2: stream util + tests
- commit 3: docs tutorial updates + troubleshooting section
- PR title: devx: tutorial/sample-app - fix streaming parse + auth guidance (closes GH #329, JIRA-DEVX-1023)

Slack/meeting notes (from quick sync 2026-03-13):
- Aisha: will prototype streaming util in the morning.
- Luca: update doc copy and add Windows note.
- Product: OK with wording but wants phrase "do not commit your keys" in bold near the env section.

Open micro-tasks (bite-sized, assignable):
- add failing unit test demonstrating current bug (good for PR signal).
- small gif or screenshot: show success flow after fix (one-liner command + output).
- update README in sample folder to explicitly call out Node >=16 and show expected output.

Final: prioritize patching the runtime parsing bug first (highest pain), then doc mismatch. Ship single PR, announce in #devx and #docs when merged.

Random notes / ideas:
- Could add a tiny `redwood devx doctor` script that checks node version and env var presence across all tutorial sample folders — useful for maintainers. Low-effort, high ROI.
- Add a note to onboarding checklist so new samples are run in matrix before merge.

---
Small personal TODO for tomorrow:
- 09:00 - implement buffer util skeleton
- 11:30 - sync with Aisha to pair on tests
- 14:00 - open draft PR and link GH issue & JIRA
- 16:00 - quick docs pass with Luca

End of scratchpad. Will tidy before PR but keeping this raw so I don't lose context.
plain_text_preview: Scratchpad: fix tutorial sample auth/stream bugs; deliver patch + docs; tests + CI; PR. Owners: Diego, Aisha, Luca. Target: ship ASAP.
